business_meaning: Unique identifier of a customer order (one row per order, duplicates removed in staging).
Customer account that placed the order; links to stg_customers.customer_id.
allowed_values_or_range: Must exist in stg_customers; observed 10001 to 20962 (14 orders have a customer_id not found in stg_customers)

business_meaning: Calendar date the customer placed the order.
allowed_values_or_range: From 2025-01-01 to today (5 rows are in the future, up to 2027-03-13: data quality issue)

business_meaning: Current fulfilment status of the order; 'canceled' is normalised to 'cancelled' in staging.
Sales channel through which the order was placed.
Country the order is delivered to.
Total amount the customer pays for the order, VAT and shipping included, before refunds (= gross revenue).
allowed_values_or_range: > 0; observed max 1400.79 (2 negative and 4 zero amounts exist: data quality issue)

business_meaning: Unique identifier of a payment event (a capture or a refund).
Order the payment belongs to; links to stg_orders.order_id.
allowed_values_or_range: Must exist in stg_orders (0 orphans today); observed 700002 to 705200

business_meaning: Date the payment was captured or refunded by the provider.
allowed_values_or_range: Observed 2025-01-01 to 2026-11-13; should be on or after the order_date (4 rows are before it: data quality issue)

business_meaning: Means of payment chosen by the customer.
Amount captured or refunded in this payment event, always positive (the direction is given by payment_status).
Last 4 digits of the payment card, used to help customers recognise a payment; never the full card number.
allowed_values_or_range: 0000 to 9999; empty when no card is involved (39% empty; also filled for some paypal / bank_transfer rows: to check with the provider)

business_meaning: Whether money was received from the customer (captured) or given back (refunded). Renamed from raw column 'status'.
